national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 164 Fourth round of India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable to be held in Singapore today
national_raw_news.content: The 4th round of India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR) will be held in Singapore today. The participating Ministers from the Indian side are Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, and Minister of State for Commerce, Industry, Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada. The mechanism of ISMR is an important platform to drive cooperation including in new and emerging areas. Its inaugural meeting was held in New Delhi in September 2022, followed by the 2nd meeting in Singapore in August 2024 and 3rd meeting in New Delhi in August 2025. Deliberations on Advanced Manufacturing, Connectivity, Digitalization, Healthcare and Medicine, Skills Development, and Sustainability, from these meetings drive the Roadmap for India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership CSP Roadmap, which was unveiled during the visit of Prime Minister of Singapore Lawrence Wong to India in September last year. The MEA said, the 4th round of ISMR will enable both sides to review the progress of various ongoing initiatives and identify avenues to further strengthen India-Singapore collaboration. The 4th edition of India-Singapore Business Roundtable that serves as a strategic and advisory forum of key business leaders will also be held along with ISMR. Meanwhile, Dr Jaishankar met his Singaporean Counterpart, Vivian Balakrishnan, on his arrival in the country yesterday. During the meeting, the two leaders had a detailed discussion on how to further deepen Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between both the nations. Dr Jaishankar later joined Mr Balakrishnan in laying the foundation stone of the new Chancery complex of the High Commission of India in Singapore. The Minister expressed confidence that the complex will reflect the new era of India- Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and further strengthen services for the Indian diaspora.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 106 US President Donald Trump declares economic warfare against Iran
national_raw_news.content: US President Donald Trump has announced a sweeping new economic warfare against Iran. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iran was given several opportunities to reach a deal with the United States but failed to do so. He said Washington will now launch an unprecedented campaign of economic warfare and isolation against Tehran. Trump also threatened economic punishment for any country helping Tehran. He warned that any country allowing its financial institutions, businesses, airports or government agencies to provide support to Tehran will also face tremendous economic consequences. The measures are expected to focus on Iran’s key economic lifelines, including oil-smuggling networks, financial transfers, exchange houses, ship registries and front companies. He urged US allies to join Washington in isolating Iran, calling the new measures an economic D-Day. Trump said the campaign is aimed at weakening Iran’s ability to finance and support activities abroad. Trump also repeated his warning that Iran will never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon. The announcement came amid rising tensions between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global oil shipments. Trump said the waterway remains open and claimed that the US naval blockade has been highly effective. Trump’s latest comments came after earlier indications that negotiations with Iran has been paused. He said talks can resume in the future but suggested that Tehran must first be ready to make a deal. Meanwhile, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States fulfill its commitments under a 14-point memorandum. These conditions include lifting the blockade, releasing frozen Iranian assets and easing sanctions on Iranian oil.

national_raw_news.title: PIB Dehradun to organise 'Vartalaap' media workshop in Chamoli on August 20 - Indiatimes
national_raw_news.content: PIB Dehradun to organise ‘Vartalaap’ media workshop in Chamoli on August 20 PIB Dehradun to organise ‘Vartalaap’ media workshop in Chamoli on August 20 Aditi Madhukar | Aug 19, 2026, 15:42 IST Share PIB Dehradun will organise the ‘Vartalaap’ regional media workshop in Gopeshwar, Chamoli, on August 20 to strengthen dialogue between local media and the government and improve awareness of welfare schemes in rural and remote areas. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Dehradun, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, will organise a regional media workshop, ‘Vartalaap’, in Gopeshwar, Chamoli, on August 20. The one-day programme will bring together print, electronic and digital media professionals working in rural and border areas. The workshop will focus on strengthening communication between local media and the government and ensuring that information about welfare schemes, policies and initiatives reaches people in remote and rural areas. The programme will be held at the District Panchayat Auditorium in Gopeshwar. ‘Vartalaap’ is among PIB’s outreach and dialogue programmes aimed at providing media professionals with factual and authentic information about government initiatives. The workshop will also provide journalists an opportunity to interact directly with government officials and subject experts and understand the implementation and local impact of various schemes. According to PIB Dehradun, the Chamoli workshop is being organised as part of efforts to mark 12 years of the Central Government’s focus on public service, governance and welfare. Discussions will include developments in infrastructure and socio-economic sectors over the past decade, along with the role of media in communicating information about public programmes. The programme will have a special focus on initiatives concerning women, farmers, youth and healthcare. Topics including women’s self-help groups, Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, National Health Mission and the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan will be discussed. GI tags and the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative will also feature in the workshop. Other subjects, including E20 fuel, are expected to form part of the discussions. Assistant Director, PIB Dehradun, Sanjeev Sundriyal, said the workshop is intended to create a stronger dialogue between the government’s information machinery and local media. He said such programmes would help journalists access reliable information on government schemes and understand how these initiatives are reaching beneficiaries at the grassroots level. national_raw_news.title: 2nd BRICS 2026 Tourism Working Group meeting held in Jaipur - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: 2nd BRICS 2026 Tourism Working Group meeting held in Jaipur; discusses advancing cooperation in skilling, seamless travel Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर 2nd BRICS 2026 Tourism Working Group meeting held in Jaipur; discusses advancing cooperation in skilling, seamless travel ANI | Updated: Aug 19, 2026 23:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 19 (ANI): The Ministry of Tourism has hosted the 2nd BRICS 2026 Tourism Working Group (TWG) Meeting in Rajasthan's Jaipur on Wednesday under India's BRICS Chairship. The meeting was chaired by Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism , Government of India. According to the Ministry of Tourism , the meeting built upon the 1st BRICS 2026 Tourism Working Group Meeting held virtually on May 25, and brought together delegates from BRICS Member States to advance cooperation across India's thematic priorities -- Artificial Intelligence and Tourism , Sustainability and Responsible Tourism , Tourism Skilling and Capacity Building, and Tourism Exchanges and Seamless Travel Facilitation. According to the release, held under the overarching theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability ", the 2nd TWG Meeting reflected upon a shared commitment to deepen tourism cooperation among BRICS Member States. The Working Group recognised tourism as an important driver of economic growth, employment, sustainable development and people-to-people exchanges, while responding to an evolving global tourism landscape shaped by technological change, changing traveller expectations and sustainability imperatives. The discussion carried forward the four thematic priorities identified under India's Chairship and outlined areas for enhanced cooperation among Member States, including responsible use of emerging technologies, sustainable and community-centred tourism, human capital development, tourism exchanges and strengthened connectivity. In his remarks to the meeting, Bhuvnesh Kumar said that the first Tourism Working Group Meeting and subsequent consultations had enabled considerable progress in furthering India's BRICS Tourism Track. He highlighted that India's Chairship has sought to advance cooperation around sustainability, skilling, seamless travel and smart tourism. He noted that the outcome of the Working Group's deliberations would provide an important basis for the BRICS Tourism Ministers' Meeting on 21 August. As part of the programme, the BRICS delegates undertook a technical visit to key tourism and heritage sites in Jaipur, including Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Amer Palace, offering them an opportunity to experience Rajasthan's rich cultural and architectural heritage.
